replies.text:
Checks (step 2 items):

1. Automated abuse of reachable endpoints — design has no sign-in, form, email/SMS or public API: exposure is "internal" and `"auth":false`. Not applicable; flooding/resource exhaustion already covered by listed threat 5.
2. Privileged session rendering other people's content — yes: "The agent reads the repository and issue comments". Already covered by listed threat 1 (hidden instructions in issue comments/repo files).
3. Privileged actions with no record — yes: "push branches using a token with write access to all repositories". Already covered by listed threat 6.
4. Cacheable personal/financial documents — design names no documents or pages; `"dataClasses":[]`. Not applicable.
5. Attacker-controlled text into logs, exports, emails, headers — design names no logging, export or email sink. Not applicable.
6. Unconfirmed-reviewer items — the shell/exfiltration/push/DoS/repudiation ones duplicate listed threats 2–6; the "runs repository build or test code" item is a distinct vector (repo content executes without any instruction being followed) and rests on design text "reads the repository and ... can run shell commands": not covered.

{
  "schema": "threatline.threatmodel.v1",
  "issueKey": "EVAL-03",
  "sketch": {
    "components": ["AI coding agent", "shell on agent host", "git push with org-wide token", "issue comment reader", "repository checkout"],
    "dataStores": ["all organisation repositories"],
    "externalServices": ["LLM provider", "git hosting"],
    "trustBoundaries": ["untrusted repository content -> agent host shell", "issue reporters -> agent prompt", "agent host -> every repository"],
    "dataClasses": ["secrets"],
    "exposure": "internal",
    "llmFeatures": true
  },
  "threats": [
    {
      "stride": "ElevationOfPrivilege",
      "title": "Repository content the agent executes runs attacker code on the agent host, no injection needed",
      "scenario": "A contributor (or anyone whose branch the agent is asked to fix) lands a malicious test helper, build hook, Makefile target or dependency manifest entry. The agent, which 'reads the repository' and 'can run shell commands', runs the project's build/test commands to check its fix, so that repository content executes directly on the agent host. Unlike comment-based prompt injection, the agent is not tricked into following text: the code simply runs, reaching the host's token with write access to all repositories and any other checkouts present.",
      "component": "Agent host shell running repository build/test code",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 5,
      "rating": { "attacker": "user", "effort": "medium", "reach": "all", "harm": "takeover" },
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "The agent reads the repository and issue comments, and can run shell commands and push branches using a token with write access to all repositories." }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V1.14.6", "V5.2.5"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-94", "CWE-829"],
      "plainLanguage": "Running a project's build or test scripts to verify a fix executes whatever code is in that project on the agent's machine, which holds a token to every repository.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Run repository build and test commands in an isolated sandbox without the org-wide token",
        "given": "an agent run that needs to build or test the repository it is fixing",
        "when": "the agent executes project-supplied commands, hooks or dependency installs",
        "then": "those commands run in an ephemeral sandbox with no access to the push token, no other repository checkouts and restricted egress, and only the resulting diff is returned to the agent"
      }
    }
  ]
}
